title: MINDEF budget debate and withdrawn $100 amendment
what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head J (Ministry of Defence) of the Estimates, in which Mr Yip Hon Weng moved and later withdrew an amendment to reduce the allocation by $100.
stage: Committee of Supply debate on Head J of the Estimates
why_it_matters: The Minister said MINDEF/SAF will build a suite of conventional, cheap-asymmetric, cyber and classified capabilities, acquire three Gulfstream G550 maritime surveillance aircraft, and scale unmanned platforms paired with manned platforms. He also said MINDEF will take care of NSmen and NSFs in consultation with the Ministry of Finance where budget space allows, regularly review NSF allowances, and do more for HOME awards, NS credits and tax incentives where possible. The debate also covered cross-domain cooperation with other agencies and new international partnerships on cyber, information warfare and critical underwater infrastructure.

key_points.point: Mr Yip Hon Weng moved an amendment to reduce the allocation for Head J by $100.
key_points.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
key_points.quote: That the total sum to be allocated for Head J of the Estimates be reduced by $100

key_points.point: Mr Yip asked how MINDEF's security risk assessment has changed over five years.
key_points.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
key_points.quote: how has MINDEF's assessment of security conflicts and risks evolved over the past five years?

key_points.point: Mr Yip asked how Total Defence is being strengthened to prepare Singaporeans for crises.
key_points.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
key_points.quote: how are we strengthening Total Defence as a whole to prepare Singaporeans for crises and contingencies?

key_points.point: Mr Yip asked how defence diplomacy widens Singapore's strategic space while safeguarding independence.
key_points.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
key_points.quote: how is defence diplomacy widening our strategic space while safeguarding our Independence?

key_points.point: Mr Vikram Nair asked whether MINDEF will refine its approach to building defence relations with key partners.
key_points.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
key_points.quote: whether MINDEF intends to refine its approach to building defence relations with key partners

key_points.point: Mr Shawn Huang asked how MINDEF/SAF will maintain relevance and value proposition amid the changing security landscape.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (West Coast-Jurong West)
key_points.quote: how MINDEF/SAF plans to maintain its relevance and value proposition amidst the evolving security landscape.

key_points.point: Ms Joan Pereira asked for an update on strategies against emerging and disruptive battlefield technologies.
key_points.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
key_points.quote: I would like to ask the Minister for an update on our strategies to guard against such emerging and disruptive technologies that can be used on the battlefield

key_points.point: Ms Poh Li San asked how SAF uses unmanned technology in training to reduce manpower reliance.
key_points.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
key_points.quote: how is SAF using unmanned technology in local and overseas training to improve effectiveness and reduce manpower reliance?

key_points.point: Ms Yeo Wan Ling asked for an update on the DIS building cyber capabilities, talent pipelines and industry-academia partnerships.
key_points.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
key_points.quote: Can the Minister provide an update on how the DIS is building deep cyber capabilities, strengthening talent pipelines, and partnering industry and academia to stay ahead of emerging threats?

key_points.point: Dr Wan Rizal asked for defence spending projections and key drivers of change.
key_points.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
key_points.quote: what is the projection for defence spending this year in absolute terms and as a share of Government expenditure and gross domestic product (GDP), and what are the key drivers of any change?

key_points.point: Mr Gerald Giam asked how MINDEF diversifies sourcing to avoid single-point supply chain failures.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: How is MINDEF diversifying and sourcing from a wider range of global partners to mitigate single point failures in the supply chain?

key_points.point: Mr Gerald Giam asked for the AGO to have full access to audit procurement milestones, variations and delivery timelines.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: ensuring the Auditor-General's Office (AGO) is given full access to audit procurement milestones, contract variations and delivery timelines.

key_points.point: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry asked how MINDEF identifies and deploys NS capabilities so service is a genuine contribution.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
key_points.quote: How is MINDEF strengthening the identification and deployment of such capabilities, so that NS becomes not just a duty fulfilled but a period of genuine contribution to our defence?

key_points.point: Mr Kenneth Tiong asked whether MINDEF will create a cyber direct entry pathway for DIS.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: Will MINDEF consider a cyber direct entry pathway for DIS, allowing mid-career industry professionals to serve in military cyber defence with adapted entry requirements and competitive compensation?

key_points.point: Mr Kenneth Tiong asked whether the Ministry will commit to at least the LQS of $1,800 for second-year NSFs.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: will the Ministry commit to at least the LQS of $1,800 for second year NSFs?

key_points.point: Mr Melvin Yong asked how MINDEF will ensure employers recognise skills acquired during NS.
key_points.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
key_points.quote: how does MINDEF intend to ensure that the skills acquired by servicemen are duly recognised?

key_points.point: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim asked how Singapore will strengthen defence cooperation with the US, China and other partners.
key_points.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
key_points.quote: How will Singapore strengthen defence cooperation not only with the US and China, but also with other key strategic partners in our region and beyond

key_points.point: Mr Lee Hong Chuang asked how MINDEF establishes clearer cooperation frameworks with other key agencies.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
key_points.quote: how does MINDEF establish clearer cooperation frameworks with other key agencies?

key_points.point: Dr Neo Kok Beng proposed redefining NS to include voluntary uniformed services.
key_points.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
key_points.quote: I would like to propose a redefining of NS to include the voluntary services of this nature, especially the uniformed groups.

key_points.point: Miss Rachel Ong asked how MINDEF sees the wider population's role in defence evolving over the longer term.
key_points.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
key_points.quote: how does MINDEF envision the role of the wider population evolving within Singapore's defence ecosystem over the longer term

key_points.point: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari asked how SAFVC will expand volunteer opportunities and new roles.
key_points.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
key_points.quote: how will SAFVC expand opportunities for volunteerism and what new roles could emerge to meet evolving operational needs from cyber and data to medical, logistics and community engagement?

key_points.point: Mr Patrick Tay asked whether SAFRA's network and facilities can engage the wider public on defence.
key_points.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
key_points.quote: Can we leverage SAFRA's network and facilities to engage the wider Singapore public on defence matters?

key_points.point: Mr Alex Yam asked how MINDEF can deepen partnerships with SAFRA beyond recreation facilities.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
key_points.quote: how MINDEF can deepen partnerships with organisations like SAFRA so that they go beyond just being facilities for recreation.

key_points.point: Mr Alex Yeo asked whether MINDEF plans to better leverage SAFRA's infrastructure and network for Total Defence awareness.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
key_points.quote: whether MINDEF have plans to better leverage SAFRA's existing infrastructure and network to build stronger ties and raise Total Defence awareness in the community.

key_points.point: Mr Chan Chun Sing set out a four-pronged approach: capabilities, commitment, contributions and connections.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: capabilities, commitment, contributions and connections.

key_points.point: Mr Chan Chun Sing said MINDEF/SAF will build conventional, cheap-asymmetric, cyber and classified capabilities.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: MINDEF/SAF will build up a suite of capabilities comprising: conventional, cheap-asymmetric, cyber and classified capabilities.

key_points.point: Mr Chan Chun Sing said the RSAF will acquire three Gulfstream G550 maritime surveillance aircraft.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: the RSAF will acquire three Gulfstream G550-Maritime Surveillance Aircraft (MSA), to complement the Boeing P-8A Maritime Patrol Aircraft.

key_points.point: Mr Chan Chun Sing said SAF will scale unmanned platforms and pair them with manned platforms.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: The SAF will also continue to scale the use of unmanned platforms for new concepts of operations and pair them with manned platforms.

key_points.point: Mr Chan Chun Sing said MINDEF will take care of NSmen and NSFs in consultation with the Ministry of Finance where budget space allows.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: We will take care of our NSmen, we will take care of our NSFs in consultation with the Ministry of Finance, where the budget space allows.

key_points.point: Mr Chan Chun Sing said MINDEF's audit system is multi-layered and robust.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: the audit system in MINDEF is multi-layered and robust.

key_points.point: Mr Chan Chun Sing said MINDEF will continue to work closely with MHA and MDDI on cross-domain threats.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: MINDEF will continue to work very closely with our MHA counterparts, MDDI.

key_points.point: Mr Chan Chun Sing said opportunities to work with new partners have expanded.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: the opportunities for us to work with new partners have also expanded.

key_points.point: Mr Chan Chun Sing said no one will partner Singapore if it is not reliable, trustworthy or capable.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
key_points.quote: nobody will partner Singapore if we are not reliable, trustworthy nor capable.

key_points.point: Mr Desmond Choo said SAFRA's vision is to move clubhouse programmes to where the people are.
key_points.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
key_points.quote: It is our vision that we will extend and move the clubhouse to where the people are.

key_points.point: Mr Yip Hon Weng withdrew his amendment.
key_points.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
key_points.quote: I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.

what_happens_next: Mr Yip Hon Weng withdrew his amendment; no further step is stated.
